newsitem.title: USA: Heir to Walgreen's drugstore chain dies.
newsitem.headline: Heir to Walgreen's drugstore chain dies.

text.p: The decomposing body of the great-grandson of the founder of the Walgreen's drugstore chain was found in his suburban Chicago apartment on Wednesday, police said.
Ted Walgreen, 36, who had a long history of drug abuse and alcoholism, was found in his apartment by the building manager, Berkeley police chief Timothy Griffin said.

Police sources said Walgreen's pet ferret may have been feeding on the body's remains, which was in an advanced state of decomposition. A neighbour said she last saw Walgreen a week earlier with a male companion.

Walgreen's father, the drugstore chain's president Charles Walgreen III, was in an unresolved well-publicised court battle with his son's estranged wife over custody of their two children. Ted Walgreen had sided with his father and stepmother in the custody fight in which they contended Lauren Walgreen was unstable and drug-addicted.
Walgreen Co is the nation's largest drugstore chain.
